title: We Didn’t Just Fall in Love… We Replaced God With It
paragraphs:
We Didn’t Just Fall in Love… We Replaced God With It
Why the Ache in Your Chest Was Never Meant to Be Filled by People
There’s a quiet confession most of us are too afraid to say out loud.
We don’t just want love…
We need it.
We chase it, build our lives around it, break ourselves trying to keep it, and when it leaves—we feel like something inside us has died.
Not hurt.
Not disappointed.
Dead.
And if you’re honest… you’ve felt that.
That moment when someone walked away and suddenly food didn’t taste the same, worship felt empty, prayers sounded hollow, and even your relationship with God felt distant.
It’s uncomfortable to admit this, but some of us don’t just crave love…
We crave it more than we crave God.
And that’s not just emotional.
That’s spiritual.
Because what we crave most… reveals what we worship.
In Deuteronomy 6:5, the command is clear:
“וְאָהַבְתָּ אֵת יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ” (Ve’ahavta et Adonai Elohecha) — “You shall love the LORD your God…”
Not partially. Not second. Not after someone else breaks your heart.
But something shifted in us.
Somewhere along the way, we started expecting people to give us what only God was designed to be.
We wanted someone to see us completely, understand us deeply, stay with us forever, and never fail us.
But that kind of love?
That’s not human.
That’s divine.
And when we demand divine fulfillment from human hearts… we crush them—and ourselves.
The truth is, many of us don’t realize we’ve turned love into an idol.
Not intentionally.
But functionally.
Because we depend on it, we prioritize it, we sacrifice for it, and we feel lost without it.
And Scripture doesn’t stay silent about this.
In Romans 1:25, Paul writes:
And that lie?
That someone else can complete what only God can sustain.
You weren’t designed to be completed by another person.
You were designed to be consumed by God.
But instead, we run toward relationships hoping they’ll fix what only repentance can heal.
We hold onto people hoping they’ll stay forever, when deep down we know only One ever promised He would.
In Matthew 22:37, Jesus says:
“ἀγαπήσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου” (agapēseis Kyrion ton Theon sou) — “Love the Lord your God…”
Before spouse. Before family. Before anyone.
Because when God is first, love becomes healthy.
But when love is first… God becomes distant.
And that’s where the ache begins.
You see it in the way we panic when someone pulls away.
You see it in the way we tolerate sin just to keep someone.
You see it in the way we compromise convictions just to not feel alone.
That’s not love.
That’s dependence.
And dependence on people will always lead to disappointment.
Because even the best people will fail you.
But God?
Never.
The Hebrew word for God’s steadfast love is “חֶסֶד” (chesed).
It’s not temporary. Not emotional. Not conditional.
It’s covenantal.
It stays when you’re unlovable.
It remains when you’re broken.
It holds when everything else falls apart.
So why do we still run to people first?
Because human love is visible.
God’s love requires faith.
And sometimes… faith feels harder than feelings.
But feelings lie.
They tell you that if someone leaves, your life loses meaning.
They tell you that being alone is the worst thing that can happen to you.
They tell you that love from people defines your worth.
But Scripture says something different.
Psalm 73:25 says:
“Whom have I in heaven but You? And earth has nothing I desire besides You.”
Read that again.
Nothing.
That’s not poetic exaggeration.
That’s spiritual alignment.
And most of us… aren’t there yet.
We still desire people more than God.
We still long for texts, attention, affection, validation.
And when we don’t get it?
We spiral.
Because somewhere deep inside… we’ve replaced God with love.
But here’s the part that might break you a little.
God isn’t asking you to stop loving people.
He’s asking you to stop needing them more than Him.
Because when you need someone more than God, you will eventually lose yourself trying to keep them.
And some of you know exactly what that feels like.
You gave everything.
You prayed for them.
You stayed when you should’ve walked away.
You ignored red flags because you were afraid of being alone.
And now?
You’re left with pieces of yourself you don’t even recognize anymore.
But this is where the Gospel breathes.
Because Jesus didn’t come just to forgive your sins.
He came to restore your order.
To take God off the second place you put Him in…
…and put Him back where He belongs.
On the throne of your heart.
Because when God is first, love stops being something you chase…
…and becomes something you receive correctly.
You stop begging for attention.
You stop settling for less.
You stop breaking yourself to keep someone who was never meant to stay.
And instead… you become anchored.
Whole.
Steady.
Not because someone loves you perfectly.
But because God already does.
“ἡμεῖς ἀγαπῶμεν, ὅτι αὐτὸς πρῶτος ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς” (hēmeis agapōmen, hoti autos prōtos ēgapēsen hēmas) — “We love because He first loved us.” (1 John 4:19)
That’s the order.
God first.
Then everything else.
So if this exposed something in you…
Be honest.
Don’t ignore it.
Sit in it.
Because healing begins where honesty starts.
You’re not alone in this.
There are thousands walking this same road—learning to love God first again.
Because this isn’t just content.
This is correction.
This is restoration.
This is discipleship.
And if you truly want to glorify God—not just emotionally, but practically—then support what is feeding your spirit.
Help this message reach more hearts.
Let your life become a testimony, not just a consumer of truth.
And if you want to go deeper…
Because staying close to truth is how you stay free.
And some of you are tired of being bound to love that keeps breaking you.
So come back.
Not to another person.
To Him.
The One you were always meant to love first.
And the One who never left.
You didn’t lose love… you misplaced it.
